newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Tung to never walk alone again.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tung to never walk alone again.

text.p: Before Tung Chee-hwa's victory on Wednesday, Hong Kong's future leader was a reclusive man who often drove himself to functions and took taxis to the office.

No longer. Following Tung's sweeping victory in the race to lead the British colony upon the handover to China next year, the Hong Kong government has assigned the 59-year-old tycoon a permanant bodyguard.
Two bodyguards escorted Tung from his office, where he had waited out the results of Wednesday's vote by a China-selected electoral college, to a nearby hall where he delivered his acceptance speech.
Tung's personal assistant Stanley Shen said bodyguards would be assigned permanently from now on.
